driver: STM32N6 CRC LL independent data register: input-assisted two-function development

source_documents: RM0486 Rev 4 chapter 26 (CRC) + memory map p.176
target.hsi_contract: RM0486 Rev 4 ch.26 CRC register interface + memory map p.176 (CRC secure base 0x56024C00)
target.safety_allocation: NOT_PROVIDED: no owner safety scope recorded for the CRC benchmark work orders

scope: Write and read the general-purpose 32-bit independent data register (CRC_IDR.IDR), using only LL_CRC_Write_IDR and LL_CRC_Read_IDR.

Caller supplies a valid CRC peripheral instance with the register interface accessible; caller-owned clock, power, security and access setup is a precondition, not implemented or inferred by these LL functions.

Within this slice no LL call occurs automatically at startup, no status-flag polling or error return is specified for valid accessible calls, and invalid pointers or inaccessible hardware are outside the supported invocation domain.
Out of scope: CRC calculation/feed, polynomial configuration, initial CRC value, reversal, calculation-unit reset, DMA, HAL, other LL functions and autonomous factory modification.

dependencies.description: Valid accessible CRC_TypeDef instance; caller owns clock/power/security setup. No invented setup sequence.
Pinned ST frozen LL header and original CMSIS device/core dependencies; target Cortex-M55 secure build.

prompt_overrides.swe1_cover: Cover only CRC_IDR.IDR write/read through the two declared functions, valid accessible-instance caller preconditions and no autonomous startup writes. No generic safe state or invented error-handling contract.
prompt_overrides.swe1_effect_rule: Write-IDR: op write to CRC_IDR.IDR with the supplied 32-bit value. Read-IDR: op no_write with CRC_IDR.IDR; read returns its current 32-bit value. No calculation/reversal requirements.
prompt_overrides.ll_api: Only void LL_CRC_Write_IDR(CRC_TypeDef *CRCx, uint32_t InData) and uint32_t LL_CRC_Read_IDR(const CRC_TypeDef *CRCx); use the frozen ST signatures. CRCx is a valid accessible instance. No implicit singleton or invented return status.
prompt_overrides.swe2_static_view: Caller -> header-only stm32n6xx_ll_crc -> CRC_IDR; caller owns accessible-instance setup. Keep only the two declared IDR functions.
prompt_overrides.swe2_dynamic_view: Caller passes CRCx and a 32-bit value to LL_CRC_Write_IDR, then passes CRCx to LL_CRC_Read_IDR and receives that stored value. No CRC calculations or configuration.
prompt_overrides.ut_example: static void ut_idr(void) { LL_CRC_Write_IDR(CRC, 0x12345678U); CHECK("UT-001", CRC->IDR == 0x12345678U); CRC->IDR = 0x87654321U; CHECK("UT-002", LL_CRC_Read_IDR(CRC) == 0x87654321U); }
prompt_overrides.ut_rule: Test all 32 IDR bits with zero, all ones and alternating values; test read independently by presetting IDR. Snapshot other registers to verify the IDR calls do not change them. Use the unchanged ST header and generated host device mapping.
prompt_overrides.target_tests: Execute IDR write/read round trips at zero, all ones and alternating 32-bit patterns through the two actual ST functions; read test also presets IDR independently. Record Renode target-simulation fidelity and caller setup limitations, not physical board verification.
prompt_overrides.integration: Write a 32-bit IDR value through LL_CRC_Write_IDR(CRC,value), then read through LL_CRC_Read_IDR(CRC), and check exact equality and untouched unrelated registers. Use boundary and alternating patterns.
prompt_overrides.requirement_example: When the caller requests an IDR write with a valid accessible CRC instance, the CRC LL driver shall write the supplied 32-bit value to CRC_IDR.IDR.
